title: Strategic Accounts Lead, Partnerships
description:

With proprietary AI built on over a decade of real property data, Hover answers age-old questions like “What will it look like?” and “What will it cost?” Homeowners, contractors, and insurance professionals rely on Hover to get fully measured, accurate, and interactive 3D models of any property - all from a smartphone scan in minutes.

At Hover, we’re driven by curiosity, purpose, and a shared commitment to serving our customers, communities, and each other. We believe the best ideas come from diverse perspectives and are proud to cultivate an inclusive, high-performance culture that inspires growth, accountability, and excellence. Backed by leading investors like Google Ventures and Menlo Ventures, and trusted by industry leaders including Travelers, State Farm, and Nationwide - we’re redefining how people understand and interact with their spaces.

Why Hover wants you 

Hover is looking for a Strategic Accounts Lead to build and own our most consequential partnerships - the manufacturers and distributors whose products and networks reach nearly every contractor in the country. This is not a traditional enterprise sales role: each agreement is unique, most are seven figures, and the shape of the deal is as much your invention as the close. You'll work directly alongside Hover's CRO and VP of Sales, structuring partnerships that don't have a template yet and pulling Product, Engineering, and Finance in to build what a given deal requires. The partnerships you land will change the trajectory of Hover's Construction organization and open categories the business hasn't entered yet.

The Strategic Accounts team is a small, senior pod inside Enterprise Sales - this role plus two Partner Managers, reporting into Strategic Accounts leadership. It's deliberately flat and high-autonomy: there's no established playbook for the partnership motion, and the person in this seat will write much of it.

You will contribute by

You will own and expand revenue across Hover's most strategic manufacturers and distributors, developing account plans that balance multi-year relationship building against near-term revenue. You will lead complex, multi-threaded sales cycles that involve executive stakeholders across several organizations at once, and build trusted relationships with C-suite executives, operating partners, and business leaders in an industry where reputation travels fast. Because these deals are structurally new, you will work closely with Product and Engineering to determine whether we already have what a deal requires or need to build it - and with Sales leadership to make sure a partnership never creates channel conflict with the broader sales motion. You will maintain forecast accuracy and operational rigor through long cycles where discipline matters more than urgency, and you will build the pipeline of strategic deals that carry the business into 2028 and beyond. You'll travel regularly (~2-3x/quarter) to meet partners, strengthen executive relationships, and represent Hover at industry events and executive forums.

A rough sense of how the week breaks down: about half your time in partner meetings and structuring deals, a quarter in internal alignment across Product, Engineering, Ops, and Finance, and the rest in follow-up and account administration.

Your background includes

• 10+ years of enterprise SaaS sales experience, with a track record of closing complex, multi-stakeholder deals

• Demonstrated success driving revenue growth within strategic or named enterprise accounts

• Experience building relationships with and selling to VP and C-suite decision makers

• Experience creating and executing structured account plans

• Strong written, verbal, and presentation skills, with the executive presence to hold a room of senior stakeholders

• Proficiency with CRM and modern sales tooling (Salesforce, LinkedIn Sales Navigator, Clay, or equivalents)

title: Freshwater Strategy Director, Asia Pacific
description:
What We Can Achieve Together:
Freshwater ecosystems around the world are in crisis - pushed to the brink by the climate crisis - resulting in a sharp and long-term decline in water security and biodiversity. Freshwater is central to The Nature Conservancy's 2030 Goals, and to our work in Asia Pacific. At TNC we have set ourselves three ambitious goals to achieve by 2030: Safeguard or restore at least 1 million kilometers of healthy rivers and streams, conserve 30 million hectares of lakes, wetlands, deltas and floodplains, and ensure over 10 million people benefit directly from healthy freshwater ecosystems. Asia Pacific will make a critical contribution to these organizational goals.
Asia Pacific holds significant water resources vital for people and natural ecosystems, and hosts unique freshwater biodiversity that requires urgent action and integrated management approaches. The Nature Conservancy works with a wide range of partners to make transformational changes, orchestrate system-wide approaches, conserve freshwater biodiversity at scale and align investments with the natural infrastructure that underlies water security. Managing water is crucial for sustained economic growth, and to avoid conflicts among water users. Nature's role in water regulation is technically well-understood but vastly underrepresented in spending.
We’re Looking for You:
The Nature Conservancy seeks an innovative leader with deep expertise in freshwater science, biodiversity conservation and/or water resource management to serve as the Freshwater Strategy Director for Asia Pacific. The Freshwater Strategy Director works for the Asia Pacific regional program to develop and support freshwater conservation strategies across the region in close partnership with TNC country and global programs. The Freshwater Strategy Director ensures TNC has an impactful portfolio of freshwater conservation projects in Asia Pacific for resilient watersheds and durable freshwater protection, enhancing, scaling, and innovating from significant existing programs within the region and across the globe. They report to the Asia Pacific Deputy Director of Conservation, but must function well in a decentralized and highly matrixed structure.
ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS & RESPONSIBILITIES
In close collaboration with the Asia Pacific Lead Scientist & Director of Conservation, staff in Country programs, and TNC Global teams, the Asia Pacific Director of Freshwater Conservation designs and supports the implementation of freshwater conservation strategies in the Asia Pacific. This includes both nature-based solutions for water provisioning and regulation, and durable freshwater protection.
They cultivate collaborative working partnerships with the Asia Pacific regional country teams and with other staff across the Conservancy and external partners to increase the pace, scale and impact of our conservation strategies. This includes aligning our work in Asia Pacific with TNC’s global teams and pathways of impact.
They improve freshwater conservation outcomes through supporting and building scientific and technical capacity with country programs in the Asia Pacific. And through refining and strengthening our Theories of Change for freshwater conservation.
They help negotiate innovative solutions with diverse stakeholders, including local communities, government agencies, corporations, and lending institutions.
They ensure freshwater conservation work across the Asia Pacific Region is strongly represented in Asia Pacific’s Portfolio Management approach, and is underpinned by robust monitoring, evaluation and learning programs that report on progress against TNC’s 2030 Goals
They are the focal point in Asia Pacific for TNC’s Nature4Water partnership.
They work closely with regional and global fundraising teams to actively pursue and secure fundraising opportunities that advance freshwater priorities - including TNC’s Forever Freshwater priority geographies in Mongolia and Australia - for Asia

title: Head of AI Automation
description:
About Dispensed

At Dispensed ,we are passionate about empowering individuals to reach their full potential by supporting better health outcomes. We believe that access to innovative and alternative therapies can transform lives. Through our telehealth platform, we facilitate patient access to affordable, efficient, and reliable alternative medicine services across Australia, NZ and the UK.

About the role

Across the business, our teams are doing manual work every day that a well-built system could take on instead. We want one person whose job is to find that work and give teams their time back by building real automation and putting it into production.

We're a telehealth business operating across Australia, the UK and New Zealand, covering patient onboarding, prescriber workflows, pharmacy fulfilment, clinical admin and patient support. We've already proven this kind of work can be automated - now we want to build it in-house.

This is a hands-on role - less overseeing, more building and delivering.

What you'll own

• Work alongside teams to identify the parts of their work that could be automated

• Build the automation, agent, tool or integration that fixes it, and get it into production

• Measure the impact - establish a baseline before you start, then track what changed

• Set the team up for success by handing over automations once they're stable, documented and the team knows how to run it

• Keep track of what's newly possible in AI and turn that into things we can stop doing manually

• Bring the AI enablement work we currently outsource in-house

Your first 90 days will focus on three areas: patient support, then clinic and prescriber operations, then pharmacy order operations. Ideally, you'll have something built and running within a month.

What you'll need

Essential:

• Proven experience building AI-powered agents, apps, automations or internal tools that saw real use

• The ability to code and deploy independently, without relying on other teams

• Solid skills in prompting, evaluation, retrieval, APIs, and data handling, plus enough security awareness to handle patient data properly

• A good instinct for finding where the real time savings are in an unfamiliar process

• The ability to earn trust with busy, non-technical operators

• Able to work without a ready-made backlog - you identify what needs doing

Nice to have:

• Experience in healthcare, telehealth or another regulated industry

• Background in forward-deployed or solutions engineering

• Founder or early-stage startup experience

Things to know before applying:

• We operate under Australian privacy law, UK GDPR and NZ requirements, plus medicinal cannabis regulation in three countries. Some automations need a different approach

• Success means what's still running six months later, not how many things were built

• This role works best when it fits naturally into how teams already operate

What We Offer

• Work From Anywhere

• A competitive salary & benefits package

• A supportive and positive work environment

How to apply

Send us your CV plus a couple of examples of what you've built - an agent, a tool, an automation. A repo, video or a short write-up. Applications without a build example won't be considered.
